Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers 1.2 Whole Numbers (25 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner
Topic 1.3: Addition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 25

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Addition, part of Numbers 1.2 Whole Numbers (25 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you add a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Safely put two groups of objects together in purposive groups/pairs and count to get the total. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to perform given tasks. Safety

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Safely put two groups of objects together in purposive groups/pairs and count to get the total. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to perform given tasks. Safety

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Addition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity: learner makes number patterns involving addition.

• Collaboration: learner plays games involving addition with peers.

Values:
Social justice: learner accommodates others as they play games involving addition.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety issues: learner safely puts two groups of objects together and counts to get the total.

● Creative thinking: learner creatively makes number patterns involving addition with numbers up to 50.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills used in writing addition sentences to functional writing in English Language Activities.
